basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

Q1.answer: (a) Documents in the series, all in 91 FR: (1) Proclamation 11046, FR Doc 2026-14991, 91 FR 46639, signed July 20, published July 23, 2026: 50% additional duty on Annex II alcoholic beverages; operative time 12:01 a.m. ET August 19, 2026, measured against goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse on or after that time (entry event; clauses (1) and (3), 46641). (2) Proclamation 11047, FR Doc 2026-14992, 91 FR 46653, signed July 20, published July 23: same structure for Annex II dairy; same August 19 entry-event date (46654-55). (3) Proclamation 11048, FR Doc 2026-14997, 91 FR 46663, signed July 20, published July 23: same for Annex II motor vehicles; August 19 entry-event date (46665). (4) Proclamation 11056, FR Doc 2026-17294, 91 FR 54789, signed August 18, filed August 21 at 11:15 a.m., published August 24: suspends the 11046-11048 duties for 3 days and sets the effective date at 12:01 a.m. August 22, 2026 (clause (1), 54790), measured by entry/withdrawal; amends the Annex II chapeau of each; refunds clause (4), 54791. (5) Proclamation 11061, FR Doc 2026-18835, 91 FR 58311, signed September 8, filed September 11, published September 14: excludes listed Canadian alcoholic beverages from importation for goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. September 29, 2026 (an import/arrival event, clause (1), 58312); goods imported before September 29 but not yet entered or withdrawn stay at 50% (clause (2)). (6) Proclamation 11062, FR Doc 2026-18836, 91 FR 58319, signed September 8, published September 14: same exclusion for dairy, effective September 29 (import event). (7) Proclamation 11063, FR Doc 2026-18837, 91 FR 58325: same exclusion for motor vehicles, effective September 29 (import event). (8) Proclamation 11064, FR Doc 2026-18838, 91 FR 58331, signed September 8, published September 14: alcoholic-beverage scope change; Annex I Part A products become subject to 50%, Part B products cease to be subject; effective 12:01 a.m. September 15, 2026 (entry/withdrawal event, clause (1), 58332). (9) Proclamation 11065, FR Doc 2026-18839, 91 FR 58339, signed September 8, published September 14: same scope change for motor vehicles (Part A added, Part B removed), effective 12:01 a.m. September 15 (entry/withdrawal event, 58340). (10) Proclamation 11076, FR Doc 2026-22292, 91 FR 68861, signed October 23, filed October 29 at 11:15 a.m., published October 30: further motor-vehicle scope change; Part A products no longer subject, Part B products subject; effective 12:01 a.m. October 30, 2026 (entry/withdrawal event, 68862). (b) Product groups: Alcoholic beverages: 11046 set the original Annex II; 11064 changed Annex I Parts A and B (from September 15); 11061 moved its Annex products into the import ban (from September 29); 11056 suspended the duties. Dairy: 11047 set the original Annex II; no scope proclamation for dairy was found; 11062 moved its Annex products into the import ban (from September 29); 11056 suspended the duties. Motor vehicles: 11048 set the original Annex II; 11065 (from September 15) added Part A and removed Part B; 11063 moved its Annex products into the import ban (from September 29); 11076 (from October 30) removed Part A products and added Part B products.
Q1.basis: FR documents cited above; operative clauses read in full text for 11046 (2026-14991), 11056 (2026-17294), 11061 (2026-18835), 11064 (2026-18838), 11065 (2026-18839), 11076 (2026-22292); the other documents were checked by grep for their effective-date and exclusion clauses. Document FR pages as printed.
Q1.uncertainty: The product lists (Annex II, Part A and Part B, and the exclusion Annexes) are images and could not be read, so product membership is taken from the descriptions in the operative clauses only. No CBP implementing notice for the Canada section 338 duties appeared in the FR search, although clause (7) of 11046 contemplates one. The 11056 suspension text sets no condition, while later documents describe the lapse as caused by Canada's August 21 conduct (see Q11).

Q2.answer: (a) Entry 1 (2:00 p.m. August 20): $0. Entry 2 (11:59 p.m. August 21): $0. Entry 3 (12:01 a.m. August 22): 50% x $40,000 = $20,000 total section 338 duty. Controlling text: clause (1) of 11046 (50% on Annex II goods entered on or after the effective date) as the effective date was reset by clause (1) of 11056 to 12:01 a.m. August 22, 2026, with the 3-day suspension in 11056 covering August 19-21; see also recital 4 of 11064 (91 FR 58331). (b) Clauses (1) and (3) of 11046 still print 'August 19, 2026' in the body. Clause (1) of 11056 states that the effective date 'shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026' and says the Annex II chapeau of each of 11046, 11047 and 11048 is amended by deleting 'August 19, 2026' and inserting 'August 22, 2026'. So the amendment is textually limited to the chapeau; the body clauses were not amended. The resolution is clause (1) of 11056, which is the later and specific text; 11064 (recital 4) and 11065 and 11076 (recital 4) confirm that the duties became effective at 12:01 a.m. August 22. (c) Clause (4) of 11056 (91 FR 54791): to the extent implementation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed under applicable law and CBP's standard procedures. The FR gives no timing, interest or claim mechanism. (d) No further presidential action was needed for the duties to begin: the start came from 11046 as altered by 11056. Clause (2) of 11056 directed agencies to suspend collection during the suspension. Later documents (recitals 3-4 of 11064, 91 FR 58331; recitals 3-4 of 11065, 58339; recitals 3-4 of 11076, 68861) say that on August 21 Canada reneged and that at 12:01 a.m. August 22 the 3-day suspension lapsed and the duties became effective. (e) The original August 19 start is 30 days after the July 20 signing of 11046 (July 20 to July 31 is 11 days; July 31 to August 19 is 19 more days; total 30). Recital 10 of 11046 (91 FR 46641) states that section 338 duties may not 'take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation finding'; the findings are in recitals 7-9 of 11046 (46640).
Q2.uncertainty: Whether the Annex II chapeau in fact printed the August 19 date cannot be verified because the Annex is an image. The 11056 text is unconditional, but 11064 describes the lapse as 'accordingly' following Canada's August 21 conduct; the documents do not explain the causal link. No CBP notice implementing the August 22 date appeared in the FR search.

Q3.answer: (a) A: May be imported (arrival September 10 is before the September 29 exclusion, 11061 clause (1)). Entry September 14 is at 50% (Annex II, clause (1) of 11046 as set by 11056): 50% x $30,000 = $15,000. B: May be imported (arrival September 27 is before September 29); withdrawal for consumption on October 5 is at 50% under clause (2) of 11061 (goods imported before September 29 but not yet withdrawn 'will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate'): 50% x $30,000 = $15,000. C: May be imported (arrival at 11:30 p.m. September 28 is before 12:01 a.m. September 29); entry at 9:00 a.m. September 29 is at 50% under clause (2) of 11061: $15,000. D: May not be imported. Arrival at 12:30 a.m. September 29 is an importation on or after the exclusion's effective time (clause (1) of 11061), so no consumption entry is possible and no section 338 duty is computed for an admitted entry. (b) Shipment E: The 50% duty applies: it was admitted to an FTZ on September 25, after the August 22 effective date, so clause (4) of 11046 requires privileged foreign status (not domestic status) and the goods are subject on entry for consumption to the duty. It was imported before September 29, so clause (2) of 11061 leaves it at 50% rather than banned. On entry for consumption from the zone on October 6 the duty is 50% x $30,000 = $15,000. (c) If the exclusion is held invalid as applied to this beer, clause (9)(b) of 11061 (91 FR 58313) provides that the 50% duty under 11046 applies to the import to which the invalidated ban had applied; no other ban or additional duty is affected. Shipments imported after the ruling would therefore bear the 50% duty of 11046 under clause (9)(b) of 11061. (d) No. Clause (3) of 11061 (58313) says the exclusion proclamation 'does not otherwise affect' products subject to 11046 other than those moved into the ban, so unlisted Canadian alcoholic products remain at 50% under 11046 as modified by 11064.
Q3.uncertainty: Whether a bonded-warehouse withdrawal or FTZ withdrawal counts as 'importation' for the exclusion is not spelled out; the reading used follows clause (2) of 11061, which expressly addresses goods imported before September 29 and withdrawn later. The Annex listing of the beer is an image and assumed by the scenario. Section 301 duty is outside this question.

Q4.answer: (a) September 10, 2026: X: section 232 = 25% x $100,000 = $25,000; section 338 = $0 (clause (2) of 11046: 50% duties 'shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232'; 91 FR 46641). Y: section 232 = $25,000; section 338 = $0 (clause (2) of 11047, 91 FR 46655, same exclusion). Z: section 232 = $25,000; section 338 = $0 (clause (2) of 11048, 91 FR 46665, same exclusion). (b) October 1, 2026: X: section 232 = $25,000; section 338 = 50% x $100,000 = $50,000, because clause (1) of 11064 (91 FR 58332) states that 'the duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11046, as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232', effective September 15. Y: section 232 = $25,000; section 338 = $0 (no dairy scope change; clause (2) of 11047 still applies). Z: section 232 = $25,000; section 338 = 50% x $100,000 = $50,000, because clause (1) of 11065 (91 FR 58340) has the same 'in addition to section 232' sentence for the motor-vehicle duties (effective September 15, and carried into 11076, 68862). (c) Text deciding each answer: exclusion of section 232 articles in clause (2) of 11046 (46641), 11047 (46655), 11048 (46665); stacking sentence in clause (1) of 11064 (58332) and clause (1) of 11065 (58340), each stating the 'as modified' duties 'shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232'; effective date sentences in those clauses (September 15, 2026, 12:01 a.m., entry or withdrawal).
Q4.basis: Clause (2) of 11046, 11047, 11048; clause (1) of 11064 and 11065; clause (1) of 11076 (68862) repeats the stacking sentence for October 30; section 232 rates per the scenario (25%).
Q4.uncertainty: The 'shall apply in addition to section 232' sentence in 11064 and 11065 does not say that it overrides clause (2) of 11046, but the later text is the more specific and the only operative statement on section 232 for the post-September 15 period. Whether the stacking sentence reaches products in Annex II that are not in Part A or B (X, Z) is not stated expressly; the reading above extends it to all duties 'imposed pursuant to' 11046 or 11048 as modified. Annex lists are images.

Q5.answer: (a) Consumption entries: P (Annex I Part A of 11065; not in original Annex II): 3:00 p.m. Sept 14: no (before 12:01 a.m. Sept 15 effective time, 11065 clause (1)); 12:01 a.m. Sept 15: yes 50%; 4:00 p.m. Oct 29: yes; 12:01 a.m. Oct 30: yes (P is not described as in Part A of 11076); Nov 3: yes. Q (original Annex II and Part B of 11065): Sept 14 3:00 p.m.: yes 50% (Part B removal not yet effective); Sept 15 12:01 a.m.: no (removed); Oct 29: no; Oct 30: no; Nov 3: no. R (original Annex II and Part A of 11076): Sept 14: yes; Sept 15: yes (Part A of 11065 does not cover R); Oct 29 4:00 p.m.: yes; Oct 30 12:01 a.m.: no (11076 clause (1): Part A products 'shall no longer be subject'); Nov 3: no. S (Part B of 11076; not earlier): Sept 14: no; Sept 15: no; Oct 29: no; Oct 30 12:01 a.m.: yes; Nov 3: yes. (b) 11076: signed October 23, 2026; filed for public inspection/Office of the Federal Register on October 29 at 11:15 a.m. (FR Doc 2026-22292 footer); published October 30, 2026 at 91 FR 68861. It applies from 12:01 a.m. eastern time on October 30, 2026 to goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse on or after that time (clause (1), 68862). It does not reach entries made before that time. Neither 11065 nor 11076 contains a refund clause (the only refund clause in this series is clause (4) of 11056). (c) P: signed September 8, 2026, effective September 15 at 12:01 a.m., 7 days later. S: signed October 23, effective October 30 at 12:01 a.m., 7 days later. Both scope documents recite that section 338 provides duties 'not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation finding' (11065 recital and 11076 recital, 58340 and 68862). Neither document explains how a 7-day effective date fits that rule. The most that can be said from the text is that the 30-day clock could be measured from the original July 20 finding in 11048 (Aug 19 earliest), and the products added later would then be well beyond 30 days; the documents do not say this.
Q5.basis: 11065 (2026-18839) clause (1) (58340); 11076 (2026-22292) clause (1) (68862), filing legend (68871); recitals on the 30-day statutory limit (11065 at 58340; 11076 at 68862); 11048 clause (1) (46665) for the original Annex II.
Q5.uncertainty: Annex I Part A and Part B lists are images, so the product assignments in the scenario are taken as given. The documents do not address the 30-day rule for scope-based additions; the explanation above is an inference, not a statement in the documents. Whether a product in Part A of 11065 is also in Part A of 11076 is not stated.

Q6.answer: Basis: adopted rates per the notice (91 FR 47318) determinations and memo section 1(a) (91 FR 47720); $100,000 customs value; MFN 4%. (1) Switzerland (net of MFN, 12.5%): 301 = 12.5% - 4% = 8.5% x $100,000 = $8,500; MFN + 301 = $4,000 + $8,500 = $12,500. (2) Norway (flat 12.5%): 301 = $12,500; total $4,000 + $12,500 = $16,500. (3) United Kingdom (flat 10%): 301 = $10,000; total $14,000. (4) Germany (EU net of MFN, 10%): 10% - 4% = 6% x $100,000 = $6,000; total $10,000. (5) Taiwan (net of MFN, 10%): $6,000; total $10,000. (6) Turkiye (flat 12.5%): $12,500; total $16,500. (7) Japan (net of MFN, 12.5%): $8,500; total $12,500. (8) Liechtenstein: not one of the 60 investigated economies (memo list, 91 FR 47717-18); section 301 duty $0; total $4,000. (9) Hong Kong (flat 12.5%): $12,500; total $16,500. (10) India (flat 10%): $10,000; total $14,000. (b) Germany, MFN 12% (EU net, MFN at or above 10%): $0. Japan, MFN 12% (net 12.5%): 0.5% x $100,000 = $500. Taiwan, MFN exactly 10%: $0. South Korea, MFN exactly 10% (net 12.5%): 2.5% x $100,000 = $2,500. Switzerland, MFN free (net 12.5%): 12.5% x $100,000 = $12,500. (c) Versus the June 5 proposal (91 FR 34274, section IV): the June text proposed flat rates with no net-of-MFN treatment. Changed treatment: EU (including Germany) moved from 10% flat to 10% net of MFN; Taiwan from 10% flat to 10% net of MFN; Japan and Switzerland from 12.5% flat to 12.5% net of MFN. India's rate changed from 12.5% (June) to 10% (adopted). Reason stated for India: India's adoption of a forced-labor import prohibition after the June 5 notice (notice, India determination, 91 FR 47324; memo recital, 47720). Unchanged: UK (10%), Norway, Turkiye and Hong Kong (12.5% flat). Liechtenstein was not a proposed economy.
Q6.basis: Memo sec. 1(a)(i)-(iii) (91 FR 47720) and the net-of-MFN language in 1(a)(ii); notice determinations: EU 91 FR 47323, Taiwan 47327, Japan 47324, Switzerland 47327, Norway 47326, Turkiye 47328, UK 47328, Hong Kong 47324, India 47324; June proposal 91 FR 34274 (section IV); the list of 60 economies 91 FR 47717-18 and 34273-74.
Q6.uncertainty: Annex I and II exemptions (images) could reduce duties for particular products; none is assumed. Whether Germany is treated as EU for the net rule follows from the EU determination ('products of the European Union') and the memo text; no separate Germany entry exists. Liechtenstein's absence from the 60-economy list is taken from the lists in the memo and notice.

Q7.answer: (a) France (EU, net of MFN 10%). Column 1 duty = $0.03 x 2,000 kg = $60; ad valorem equivalent = $60 / $12,000 = 0.5%. Section 301 = (10% - 0.5%) x $12,000 = 9.5% x $12,000 = $1,140. (b) Column 1 duty = 4% x $20,000 ($800) + $0.25 x 4,000 kg ($1,000) = $1,800; AVE = $1,800 / $20,000 = 9%. Italy (EU net, 10%): (10% - 9%) x $20,000 = $200. Japan (net, 12.5%): (12.5% - 9%) x $20,000 = $700. Brazil (flat 12.5%, no net rule): 12.5% x $20,000 = $2,500. (c) Column 1 duty $2,200 / $20,000 = AVE 11%. Taiwan (net, 10%): AVE is at or above 10%, so section 301 = $0. Switzerland (net, 12.5%): (12.5% - 11%) x $20,000 = 1.5% x $20,000 = $300. (d) The rule for non-ad valorem MFN rates is U.S. note 52(k) (the note text printed with the Annex I HTSUS modifications, 91 FR 47394 area): for goods of EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland or Taiwan with a specific or compound column 1-General rate, the AVE equals column 1 duty divided by customs value (example at 47394). The result where the AVE is at or above the cap is stated in the chapter 99 headings' rule (for the 10% and 12.5% headings, the sum is set at the cap only where the column 1 duty is less than the cap; 47394), and in the memo (section 1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720: section 301 tariff of zero where the MFN tariff is at or above the cap) and the notice's EU and Japan determinations (91 FR 47323-24, same).
Q7.basis: Notice (2026-15181) U.S. note 52(k) text at 91 FR 47394; memo section 1(a)(ii) (47720); determinations for EU (47323), Japan (47324), Switzerland (47327), Taiwan (47327); HTSUS chapter 99 headings text (47394).
Q7.uncertainty: The zero result at or above the cap is clearly stated in the memo and determinations but for the chapter 99 headings only by implication ('less than' language). Column 1 rates for the scenario products are assumed to be as given.

Q8.answer: Rate: Dominican Republic determination, 12.5% flat ad valorem (91 FR 47323); duty = 12.5% x $80,000 = $10,000 per shipment unless excluded. (1) Loaded July 22 on a vessel, in transit before July 24, entered July 29 (after July 28): exemption does not apply: $10,000. (2) Entered July 27 at 3:00 p.m. (loaded July 22, in transit, entered before 12:01 a.m. July 28): exempt: $0. (3) Entered 12:01 a.m. July 28: not before 12:01 a.m. July 28, so not exempt: $10,000. (4) Loaded July 24 at 6:00 a.m.: not loaded before July 24, so no in-transit exemption; entered July 27 after the effective time: $10,000. (5) Entered July 23, before 12:01 a.m. July 24: $0. (6) Withdrawn from bonded warehouse July 26, on or after July 24: $10,000 (the in-transit exemption does not reach goods in a warehouse). (7) Air freight loaded on an aircraft at 9:00 p.m. July 23, entered July 25: the exemption in the DATES line is limited to goods 'loaded onto a vessel', so as written it does not cover air freight: $10,000 (see uncertainty). (b) The in-transit rule is in the DATES line of the notice, 91 FR 47318. (c) Memorandum of July 23, 2026 (FR Doc 2026-15274, 91 FR 47717), published July 28, 2026. USTR notice of action (FR Doc 2026-15181, 91 FR 47318), published July 28, 2026. Duties apply to goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time July 24, 2026 (DATES, 47318). (d) Patented pharmaceutical articles in 9903.04.60-9903.04.66 were added to the note 52(f) exemption list effective 12:01 a.m. July 31, 2026 (Annex I, part B, 91 FR 47394; note 52(f)(8)). July 30 entry: not exempt, $10,000. August 3 entry: exempt, $0.
Q8.basis: Notice DATES line (91 FR 47318); Dominican Republic determination (47323); Annex I part B and note 52(f)(8) (47394); memo signed July 23 (47717); publication dates from the FR index.
Q8.uncertainty: The aircraft case (item 7) depends on whether 'vessel' in the DATES line includes aircraft; the text as printed does not say so and the document has no definition, so the result given is the literal reading. Annex I images could add a product-specific exemption for these goods; none is assumed. The ten-item DATES sentence on in-transit goods was read from the printed text.

Q9.answer: (a) Thailand (flat 12.5%) applies to the value of the assembled article less the U.S. content under 9802.00.80: ($100,000 - $35,000) x 12.5% = $65,000 x 12.5% = $8,125. (b) Israel repairs, subheading 9802.00.50: the duty applies to the value of repairs only: $6,000 x 12.5% = $750. (c) Mexico (flat 10%): (i) USMCA duty-free entry: $0, because heading 9903.05.55 does not apply to Mexican products entered free of duty under the USMCA (note 52(h), 91 FR 47363). (ii) No USMCA claim: 10% x $50,000 = $5,000. (d) Passenger car under 9903.94.01: $0; note 52(f)(2) (91 FR 47362) excludes passenger vehicles provided for in 9903.94.01 from the section 301 duty. (e) Brazil (flat 12.5%): 12.5% x $100,000 = $12,500; note 52(f) lists only specified section 232 headings (for example 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04-9903.82.26, 9903.94 and others), so a section 232 heading not mentioned in the note does not exempt the article. (f) June proposal (91 FR 34274): proposed exemptions included 'all articles and parts currently subject to section 232 tariffs', informational materials (for example books), donations and accompanied baggage (34274, section IV; also restated at 47318). Adopted text: the section 232 exemption is limited to the headings listed in note 52(f) (47362-63), not all section 232 articles; note 52(a) (47352) excludes accompanied-baggage items only where they are 'products for personal use'; informational materials and donations do not appear in the readable adopted text (any treatment would be in the Annex images).
Q9.basis: Notice note 52(a) (91 FR 47352), 52(f) (47362-63), 52(g), (h) (47363); June proposal 91 FR 34274; notice overview 47318; 9802 rule in note 52(a) (47352); passenger vehicle rule note 52(f)(2) (47362).
Q9.uncertainty: Annex images may exempt or add products (including informational materials and donations); those rules are outside this answer. Brazil's rate is from its determination (47322). For item (c)(i), the scenario's USMCA claim is assumed valid.

Q10.answer: Scenario 1 (aluminum extrusions, 232 heading 9903.82.02, Annex II motor vehicles, MFN 3%, value $200,000): (a) September 10, 2026: MFN = 3% x $200,000 = $6,000; section 232 = 50% x $200,000 = $100,000; section 338 = $0 (clause (2) of 11048 excludes section 232 articles); section 301 = $0 (note 52(f)(1) excludes articles of aluminum in 9903.82.02). Total $106,000. (b) September 16, 2026: MFN $6,000; section 232 $100,000; section 338 = 50% x $200,000 = $100,000 (clause (1) of 11065 'shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232', effective September 15); section 301 $0. Total $206,000. Scenario 2 (rye whisky, Annex II alcohol, value $60,000, MFN free): (c) USMCA duty-free entry on September 1: section 338 = 50% x $60,000 = $30,000 (11046 contains no USMCA exemption); section 301 = $0 (note 52(g): 9903.05.29 does not apply to Canadian goods entered free under USMCA); total $30,000. (d) No USMCA claim on September 1: section 338 $30,000; section 301 = 10% x $60,000 = $6,000 (Canada, 10%, notice 91 FR 47322); total $36,000. (e) Arrival October 2, 2026: the product is excluded (imported on or after September 29, clause (1) of 11061). No entry, so section 338 $0, section 301 $0, total $0. (f) Client question: The FR shows no 2026 document ending the Canada IEEPA duties (EO 14193, 90 FR 9113, as amended by EO 14325, 90 FR 37957, which set 35% from August 1, 2025 for non-USMCA Canadian goods). The USMCA exemption from those duties is in CBP notice 90 FR 11743 (effective March 7, 2025). Under the stacking text of EO 14289 section 3(a)(ii) (90 FR 18908) and CBP notice 90 FR 21487 (paragraph (2)), an article subject to IEEPA tariffs is not subject to the section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs. The 10% temporary import surcharge (91 FR 9339, clause (1), effective 12:01 a.m. February 24, 2026) runs for 150 days to 12:01 a.m. July 24, 2026 (9343), and no extension appeared in the FR search. So for September 2026 the surcharge is not in force; the IEEPA position depends on whether EO 14325 remains in effect, which the FR search could not establish.
Q10.uncertainty: The IEEPA status in September 2026 is not resolved by the FR; the answer reports what the FR records show. The surcharge's exclusion of section 232 articles is relevant only to aluminum products (Scenario 1 is not subject to the surcharge because it is a section 232 article). The Canadian Annex exemptions for rye whisky and the 10% section 301 rate assume no product-specific exemption.

Q11.answer: Discrepancies found (each listed once): (1) Section 232 stacking. Clause (2) of 11046 (91 FR 46641), 11047 (46655), 11048 (46665): the 50% duties 'shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232'. Clause (1) of 11064 (91 FR 58332), clause (1) of 11065 (58340), and clause (1) of 11076 (68862): the duties 'as modified' 'shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232'. The later scope documents do not say they override clause (2); the conflict is not resolved on the face of the documents. (2) Body text of 11046 versus 11056. Clauses (1) and (3) of 11046 (46641) still read 'on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 19, 2026'. Clause (1) of 11056 (54790) says the effective date 'shall be' August 22 and says the amendment is to the chapeau of Annex II only, so the body text of 11046 was not changed though the description of the change reads as an overall date change. (3) Cause of the August 22 start. Clause (1) of 11056 (54790) fixes August 22 with no condition; recitals 3-4 of 11064 (58331) and 11065 (58339) say that 'on August 21, 2026, Canada reneged' and that 'accordingly' the suspension 'lapsed' at 12:01 a.m. August 22. The operative text makes no reference to Canada's conduct. (4) FTZ clause keyed to the effective date. Clause (4) of 11046 (46641) applies to goods admitted to an FTZ 'on or after the effective date of this proclamation'. Clause (1) fixes that effective date at August 19, while the operative effective date became August 22 by 11056. (5) Notice on the list of exemptions. The notice's section D.2 heading says USTR determined 'to remove certain products from the proposed exemption list' (91 FR 47330), but the text describes limiting exemptions for certain chemicals to pharmaceutical applications, which the notice says is 'consistent with the proposal in the June 5, 2026 FRN' (47330); the June Annex A is an image and the statement cannot be checked. (6) Proposal description. The notice (47318) says the June proposal included exemptions for 'all articles and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232', which matches the June text (34274); the adopted note 52(f) is narrower (see Q9(f)); the notice does not describe that narrowing as a change.
Q11.uncertainty: Items (1) and (3) are the clearest conflicts. Item (5) cannot be verified because the annexes are not readable. The notice's section D descriptions reflect the chapter 99 text as printed; I could not read every page of the notice's section E.

Q12.answer: Section 301 duty = rate x $ value (adopted rates: Cambodia 10%, Malaysia 10%, Bangladesh 10%, Argentina 10%, Taiwan net 10%, Japan net 12.5%, Indonesia 10%, Mexico 10% flat, Thailand 12.5% flat, EU/Italy net 10%, El Salvador 10%). (a) Aloe etc. (Jordan exemption in note 52(j) applies only to Jordan): Cambodia 10% x $60,000 = $6,000; Malaysia 10% x $60,000 = $6,000. (b) Boswellia, $100,000: Malaysia $10,000; Taiwan (net, MFN 0): 10% x $100,000 = $10,000; Bangladesh $10,000; Argentina $10,000. (c) Argan oil, $100,000, MFN 4%: Taiwan (net 10%): 6% x $100,000 = $6,000; Japan (net 12.5%): 8.5% x $100,000 = $8,500; Indonesia (flat 10%): $10,000. (d) Sesame seeds for sowing, $50,000, MFN 2%: Japan (net 12.5%): 10.5% x $50,000 = $5,250; Mexico (flat 10%, no USMCA claim): $5,000; Thailand (flat 12.5%): $6,250. (e) Psyllium seed husks, $40,000: Cambodia (MFN free, 10%): $4,000; Thailand (flat 12.5%): $5,000; El Salvador (10%): $4,000; Italy (EU net, MFN 2%): 8% x $40,000 = $3,200. Note: note 52(j) exempts psyllium and aloe only for Jordan (91 FR 47394), so the Cambodia, El Salvador and Italy entries are not exempt.
Q12.basis: Determinations (notice 2026-15181): Cambodia 47322, Malaysia 47325, Bangladesh 47322, Argentina 47321, Taiwan 47327, Japan 47324, Indonesia 47324, Mexico 47325, Thailand 47327, El Salvador 47323, EU 47323; note 52(j) (47394); note 52(h) (Mexico, 47363); memo sec. 1(a) (47720).
Q12.uncertainty: Annex I and II exemptions (images) may cover some of these subheadings; none is assumed. Whether any of the listed products is subject to a particular USMCA or textile TRQ is outside these entries. Taiwan and EU net-of-MFN treatment applied as in the adopted text.

Q13.answer: Basis for all: Proclamation 11032 (FR Doc 2026-11314, 91 FR 34087): clause (2)(a) 25% for Annex I-C products unless a lower rate applies; clause (2)(d): for products of Canada/Mexico qualifying under USMCA, 25% applies only to non-U.S. content (total value minus value attributable to parts produced in the U.S.), with a floor that the total effective duty is not less than 15% (Annex IV); clause (2)(b): for Japan etc., column 1 rate topped to 15%; CBP guidance (FR Doc 2026-20938, 91 FR 65162) defines U.S. content (including U.S.-smelted metal not in U.S.-produced parts) and applies to entries on or after October 14, 2026. (a) USMCA claim, $60,000 U.S. parts, entry October 20: non-U.S. content $140,000 x 25% = $35,000; floor 15% x $200,000 = $30,000; section 232 duty = $35,000. (b) USMCA claim, no U.S. content, October 20: 25% x $200,000 = $50,000. (c) Not USMCA-qualifying, Canada: clause (2)(a) 25% x $200,000 = $50,000. (d) Japan, column 1 2.5%: clause (2)(b) tops the sum to 15%, so the additional rate is 12.5% x $200,000 = $25,000. (e) USMCA claim, $20,000 U.S. parts plus $30,000 U.S.-smelted aluminum in a Canadian part, October 20: U.S. content = $20,000 + $30,000 = $50,000 under the CBP guidance; non-U.S. content $150,000 x 25% = $37,500 (above the $30,000 floor): $37,500. (f) Same as (e) entered October 6: CBP guidance is effective only for entries on or after October 14 (2026-20938, 65162); on the proclamation text alone, the value attributable to U.S.-produced parts is $20,000, so non-U.S. content = $180,000 x 25% = $45,000 (above floor): $45,000 (see uncertainty). (g) USMCA claim, $140,000 U.S. parts: non-U.S. content $60,000 x 25% = $15,000, raised to the 15% floor of $30,000: $30,000. (h) The treatment in (a) applies to goods entered on or after June 8, 2026 until 11:59 p.m. December 31, 2027 (clause (2) of 11032). From 12:01 a.m. January 1, 2028, clause (3)(a) of 11032 applies the rates in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021 (25% unless a lower UK or U.S.-smelted rate applies, 11021 at 18204), so a full-value 25% rate would apply to Annex I-C steel products, with no USMCA content deduction.
Q13.uncertainty: (e) and (f) depend on whether U.S.-smelted aluminum in a Canadian part reduces the non-U.S. content; the proclamation's text deducts only parts produced in the U.S., so the answer for October 6 (f) follows the proclamation text, while the CBP guidance (effective only October 14) would give the lower result. Annex IV (floor and content rules) is an image. For (h), clause (3)(a) of 11032 refers to 11021's clause (3), which is written for Annex I-B and copper; the application to Annex I-C steel is an inference from 11032's cross-reference.

Q14.answer: 1. Incorrect. The memo does not give USTR until September 1. Section 2 directs TRQs 'as soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible' (91 FR 47721). September 1 appears only in the recital reporting USTR's advice that TRQs 'will be feasible by September 1, 2026' (47719-20). 2. Incorrect. The memo says USTR received over 1,600 written comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses (47719); the notice's section III says over 100 witnesses (47328). 3. Partly correct, mostly incorrect. Of the seven economies, Cambodia and Guatemala were already at 10% in the June proposal (June text, 91 FR 34274, listing them under ART commitments). Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago and Jordan moved from 12.5% to 10%. Jordan's basis was an ART commitment, not a ban (memo, 47720). 4. Incorrect. USTR 'determined not to remove' beef, avocados, paprika and the other listed products (notice, 91 FR 47331). 5. Incorrect as to Japan and South Korea: their net-of-MFN determinations cite only Annex I and Annex II Part A (47324, 47327), while EU, Switzerland and Taiwan cite additional parts (C, D, K). 6. Partly correct: 471 additional products were excluded in each investigation (47331), but the list says 'certain sugar and sugar containing products' (47331-32), not all sugar. 7. Incorrect. No statement says no product bears more than 12.5% in total; for flat economies (Norway, Hong Kong, Turkiye, Brazil, Thailand) the 12.5% is added to MFN (notice determinations, 47322-28). 8. Correct: notice, 91 FR 47321 (domestic-status exception under 19 CFR 146.43; other products admitted only as privileged foreign status). 9. Correct: memo sec. 4(e) (91 FR 47722-23): the invalidated exemption's goods become subject to the tariff action. 10. Correct as far as the readable text goes: the only limitation stated is the chemicals exemption limited to pharmaceutical applications (notice, 91 FR 47330); the Annex images could not be read.
Q14.uncertainty: Item 5 depends on the content of the Part A annex, which is an image. Item 10 depends on whether any Annex A change in the annexes is not described in the text. The June proposal's exact Annex A content cannot be read.

Q15.answer: Frame: Case N (not USMCA) vs Case U (USMCA claimed). Rates: IEEPA Canada 25% (EO 14193, 90 FR 9113, effective Feb 4, 2025), 35% from Aug 1, 2025 (EO 14325, 90 FR 37957); USMCA exemption from March 7, 2025 (CBP 90 FR 11743); section 232 aluminum 25% from March 12, 2025 (Proc. 10895, notice 90 FR 11251), 50% from June 4, 2025 (Proc. 10947, 90 FR 24200); April 6, 2026 heading 9903.82.02, Annex I-A, 50% (Proc. 11021, clause (2)(a), 91 FR 18203-04). Stacking under EO 14289 section 3(a)(ii) (90 FR 18908), effective from its signing on April 29, 2025: an article subject to IEEPA duties under 2(b)/(c) is not subject to 232 duties under 2(d)/(e). Section 301 forced labor: section 301 duty does not apply to 9903.82.02 aluminum articles (note 52(f)(1), 91 FR 47362). Section 338 motor vehicles: from Aug 22, 2026 for Annex II products; excludes section 232 articles (clause (2), 11048); from Sept 15 stacks on 232 (11065 clause (1)). Surcharge (91 FR 9339) 10%: Feb 24-July 24, 2026; excludes section 232 articles (exception (k)). Results: 1. Feb 10, 2025: N IEEPA 25% $25,000; U IEEPA 25% $25,000 (no USMCA exemption until Mar 7); 232 not yet effective. 2. Mar 6, 2025: N IEEPA $25,000; U IEEPA $25,000 (exemption not yet in effect). 3. Mar 10, 2025: N IEEPA $25,000; U $0 (USMCA exemption). 232 not yet effective (Mar 12). 4. Mar 14, 2025: N IEEPA $25,000 + 232 25% $25,000 = $50,000 (no non-stacking rule existed until EO 14289, April 29, 2025); U 232 $25,000. 5. June 3, 2025: N IEEPA $25,000 (232 not owed under EO 14289 3(a)(ii)); U 232 $25,000. 6. June 10, 2025: N IEEPA $25,000 (232 50% not owed); U 232 $50,000. 7. March 2, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000 (232 not owed; surcharge excluded as a 232-listed article, flagged); U 232 $50,000 (surcharge and IEEPA not owed). 9. June 10, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000; U 232 $50,000 (surcharge excluded). 10. July 27, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000; U 232 $50,000; section 301 not owed (note 52(f)(1)); surcharge expired July 24. 11. Aug 25, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000 + section 338 50% $100,000 = $135,000 (232 not owed, so 338 exclusion in clause (2) of 11048 does not apply; flagged); U 232 $50,000 (338 not owed while 232 applies before Sept 15). 12. Sept 14, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000 + 338 $100,000 = $135,000; U 232 $50,000 (338 excluded). 13. Sept 16, 2026: N IEEPA $35,000 + 338 $100,000 = $135,000; U 232 $50,000 + 338 $100,000 = $150,000 (stacking reading of 11065 clause (1)). 14. Q15.uncertainty: The EO 14289 stacking text, read literally, makes IEEPA duties exclude the 232 steel/aluminum duties for non-USMCA goods; the usual understanding is the reverse, and the FR record does not explain it. Whether EO 14289 covers Proc 10895 (aluminum 2025) as a 'subsequent amendment' of Proc 9705 is not stated. The status of EO 14193/14325 in 2026 is not resolved by the FR search (no termination found). The surcharge's treatment of non-USMCA 232-listed articles is not certain. Whether section 338 applies to a non-USMCA aluminum article where IEEPA rather than 232 is the applicable duty follows from the text of clause (2) of 11048 but is not spelled out. Canada-specific aluminum rules in the 2025 232 proclamations were not read in full. The Annex I-A listing is taken from the scenario.
